items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: So I furnished the rhythm section for them... Joe Newman and Illinois came down together... I went and joined the band.

ctx.x: It was the fact that I had a family, and I had a wife and two children, and I had to have something that I could take home to pay the rent and the food thing.

So anyway, I left and I came back to Washington. I had been here about I guess three weeks, maybe a month... No, it wasn't, it was about three weeks. And I got this call from Illinois Jacquet. I had met him earlier, right after I had left the Eckstine band, because around that same time he had just left the Basie band, and he came down to Washington by himself. He came down and he contacted me to get a rhythm section for him, which I got myself, I got Tommy Potter, and I think the drummer was this same fellow,…

So this was a kind of a feeler for Illinois, I guess, for the record people and agents to find out what kind of drawing power he had. Because he had been with the Basie band and with Lionel Hampton, "Flying Home" and all that, and also Cab Calloway. So he went back and he formed this eight-piece
